H01.H1: Low-Level Software Engineering for Complex Systems
H01.Supporting description: Windows and Linux kernel development, embedded firmware, embedded Linux, and C/C++ systems programming for products that work with hardware. Share your requirements or an existing system problem.

H02.Introduction: Choose the engineering work your system needs, from operating system components to device firmware and system software.

H02.1.Summary: Windows kernel components and device drivers for hardware integration, device communication, and system-level behavior.

H02.2.Summary: Firmware for microcontrollers and devices running an RTOS. Embedded Linux development for board support, system images, and user-space integration.

H02.3.Summary: Linux kernel development for device interfaces and kernel-level behavior. C/C++ systems programming for the surrounding services and software components.
H02.3.Visible capability chips: Linux Kernel; C; C++; Device Interfaces; Systems Software

H03.Description: Explore related service areas and the interfaces between them. Select a node to open its service page.

H04.Introduction: A project-specific process for defining, developing, and checking the work. Scope and deliverables are agreed around the system requirements.
H04.Stage 01: Discover: Review the target platform, existing software, and expected behavior. Agree the problem and the information needed to scope the work.
H04.Stage 02: Architect: Define component responsibilities, interfaces, and dependencies around the system requirements.
H04.Stage 03: Prototype: Investigate uncertain hardware or software behavior before committing to the full implementation.
H04.Stage 04: Implement: Develop the agreed components and their integration with the target system.
H04.Stage 05: Validate: Test the delivered behavior against agreed requirements using appropriate software checks and hardware measurements.
H04.Stage 06: Release: Prepare the agreed build, packaging, and handover materials. Address applicable signing or update requirements within the scope.
H04.Stage 07: Support: Agree who will investigate reported issues, provide fixes, and maintain the software after release.

H05.Description: Technology choices depend on the hardware, operating system, and requirements of the project.
H05.Windows: KMDF; WDM; WinDbg; WDK; Win32; ETW; WFP
H05.Embedded: STM32; ESP32; RP2040; ARM Cortex-M; Raspberry Pi; FreeRTOS; Zephyr
H05.Hardware: Oscilloscope; Logic Analyzer; JTAG; SWD; PCB
H05.Protocols: UART; SPI; I2C; CAN; USB; Bluetooth; Wi-Fi; PCIe

H06.Introduction: Start with the system, the observed behavior, and the conditions that cause the problem.

H06.1.Body: A driver crashes, a device disconnects, or an operation fails under load. Identify a reproducible failure and define how the underlying issue will be investigated.

H06.2.Body: A board needs firmware before its peripherals and application behavior can be tested together. Define the hardware inputs, interfaces, and expected device behavior.

H06.3.Body: A device interface needs kernel-level development or investigation. Define the target hardware, kernel version, and expected behavior before deciding what changes are needed.

H06.4.Body: Services and software components need a clear communication contract. Define data ownership, request handling, and failure behavior so the parts can be developed and tested together.

H07.Paragraph: Tell us about your target platform, existing code, and the behavior you need to achieve. We can discuss the scope and information needed to plan the work.

A01.H1: A Pakistan-based company dedicated to low-level software engineering.
A01.Hero description: Haeman Tech focuses on Windows and Linux kernel development, embedded firmware, embedded Linux, and C/C++ systems programming. Windows applications complement this work where a project needs a desktop interface or supporting service.

A02.H2: Software Engineering Close to the Hardware
A02.Paragraph 1: Haeman Tech was founded by Muneeb Irfan and is led by Chief Executive Officer Bedřich Said. Based in Pakistan, Haeman Tech works on software that connects operating systems, devices, and the components around them. The focus is on kernel development, embedded software, and C/C++ systems programming.
A02.Paragraph 2: Linux kernel development addresses code and interfaces within the kernel. Embedded Linux development addresses the wider device platform, including board support, system images, and user-space integration. These scopes can overlap on a device, but the work and acceptance criteria need to be defined explicitly.
A02.Paragraph 3: An engagement starts with the target platform, available hardware, existing software, and expected behavior. These inputs help define the scope, integration responsibilities, development milestones, and testing required for the work.

A03.H2: Define the System, Interfaces and Tests
A03.Principle 1: System Constraints: Understand the operating system, hardware, and expected behavior before defining the implementation.
A03.Principle 2: Clear Interfaces: Agree component responsibilities, communication contracts, and integration assumptions.
A03.Principle 3: Testable Requirements: Define how the delivered behavior will be checked, using software tests and hardware measurements where appropriate.
A03.Principle 4: Project Communication: Discuss technical decisions, dependencies, and unresolved questions at agreed review points.
A03.Principle 5: Practical Handover: Agree the source code, build, configuration, and test documentation deliverables, together with release and maintenance responsibilities.

A04.1.Description: Windows kernel components and device drivers for hardware integration, device communication, and operating system behavior.

A04.2.Description: Linux kernel components and device driver interfaces, scoped to the target hardware, kernel version, and required kernel-level behavior.

A04.3.Description: Firmware for microcontrollers and RTOS-based devices, covering peripheral communication, device behavior, and integration with the hardware.

A04.4.Description: Board support, system images, boot configuration, and user-space integration for devices running Linux. Any kernel changes are identified and scoped explicitly.

A04.5.Description: C/C++ software for system interfaces, background components, and device communication. Windows application development complements this work when a desktop interface or control panel is needed.

A06.Paragraph: Share your target platform and the engineering problem you need to address. We can discuss the scope, dependencies, and information needed to plan the work.
